To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the TCP behavior across multihops is different than the TCP behavior across a single hop; (2) the TCP behavior is different for different TCP implementations and (3) the TCP behavior depends on the wireless channel conditions.
TCP flows over multihop wireless ad hoc networks and wired Internet are unstable, unfair and inefficient.
TCP connections across multihop, 802.11 wireless networks are unstable and unfair.
In summary, our research is concerned with
TCP behavior across multihom wireless networks and the Internet.
understanding and improving the performance of TCP over wireless ad hoc networks.
TCP performance across multihop 801.11 networks and the wired network.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TCP across 802-11 ad hoc networks suffers from a serious instability problem.
the TCP behavior in the wired/wired scenario is very similar to the behavior observed in the single-hop wireless case.
the TCP behavior in ad hoc multihop networks is very different than in wired networks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a set of TCP parameters that can be adjusted to achieve good performance in the wired/wired environment.
we have identified the causes of the instability of TCP across 11 ad hoc networks.

the instability of TCP across multihop ad hoc wireless networks and the Internet is due to the interplay of three effects: (1) the lack of fairness in TCP's congestion control mechanism, (2) the lack of coordination between TCP and the MAC protocol in wireless networks, and (3) the lack of end-to-end reliability in the wireless domain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the instability of TCP flows across the wired and wireless domains can be eliminated by the use of a simple modification of TCP's congestion avoidance mechanism.
TCP is not a suitable transport layer protocol for ad hoc wireless networks.

the instability of the TCP flows is due to a combination of factors: the lack of a proper congestion control mechanism in the wireless domain, the lack of fairness in the 802.11 MAC layer and the lack of fairness among competing TCP connections.
